name: back_to_back_ebbs
prose: Test function back_to_back_ebbs() (back_to_back_ebbs_test.c:62-101), run through test_harness in a forked child whose exit status becomes the test result. It takes no parameters. SKIP_IF(!ebb_is_supported()) prints a skip message and returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99), which test_harness turns into a reported skip with status 0, before any event is opened. Otherwise it initialises an event for config 0x1001e ("cycles") as an EBB leader with exclude_kernel, exclude_hv and exclude_idle set, and FAIL_IF (which prints and returns 1) applies to: event_open failing (nothing installed yet), ebb_event_enable failing (handler installed via setup_ebb_handler, sample_period still unset, event left open), core_busy_loop returning nonzero inside the wait loop (event open, sample_period 5, PMC1 programmed, EBB globally enabled and PMCs unfrozen, none of that undone), and the final check ebb_count != NUMBER_OF_EBBS (50), which is reached after the loop, ebb_global_disable, ebb_freeze_pmcs, dump_ebb_state and event_close. Between the open and the wait loop it sets sample_period = 5, freezes the PMCs, loads PMC1 with pmc_sample_period(5), enables EBBs globally and unfreezes the PMCs. The loop runs core_busy_loop while ebb_state.stats.ebb_count < 50; the handler ebb_callee increments the count. The function returns 0 only when it ends with ebb_count exactly 50; an overshoot above 50 would return 1 through the last FAIL_IF.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (final mismatch returns after event_close and global disable, not with the event open; enable failure occurs before sample_period = 5) right (back_to_back_ebbs_test.c:79-98); round 15 (SKIP_IF returns 0 so skip path gives zero status and the function can return 0 without 50 EBBs) wrong at function level, the function returns 99 (utils.h:160-166, MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE = 99), though test_harness reports a skip with status 0 (harness.c:125-128); formal-contract claims (original, round 1) moot, no contract now. Old prose said the skip terminates 'with a nonzero status', which is wrong too. Tally 1 right 1 wrong.

name: event_alternatives_tests_p9
prose: Test function event_alternatives_tests_p9() (event_alternatives_tests_p9.c:25-111), run through test_harness in a forked child. It returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99, reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) when platform_check_for_tests() is nonzero, when PVR_VER(mfspr(SPRN_PVR)) != POWER9, or when check_for_generic_compat_pmu() is nonzero, before opening anything. Then, five times, it initialises a leader event (PM_RUN_CYC_ALT with EventCode_1, PM_INST_DISP with EventCode_2, PM_BR_2PATH with EventCode_2, PM_LD_MISS_L1 with EventCode_3, PM_RUN_INST_CMPL_ALT with EventCode_4), opens it with event_open, opens the second event as a sibling with event_open_with_group(&event, leader.fd), and closes both with event_close. Each open is wrapped in FAIL_IF, which prints a message and returns 1 immediately, so a failing leader open leaves the earlier completed pairs closed and nothing of the current pair open, and a failing sibling open leaves that pair's leader open and not closed. The function returns 0 after all five pairs succeeded; the results of event_close are not checked.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose claims all opened events are closed before returning but FAIL_IF returns early without closing) right for the current pair only (earlier pairs are closed, lines 55-56, 68-69, 81-82, 94-95); round 2 (SKIP_IF returns 0, not nonzero) wrong, it returns 99 (utils.h:158-166); round 15 (SKIP_IF returns the skip value, nonzero, not 0) right in that sense; the old prose said it returned 0 on skip and that every already-opened event leaks, both wrong or overstated. Formal-contract claims moot. Tally 2 right 1 wrong.

name: group_constraint_thresh_cmp
prose: Test function group_constraint_thresh_cmp() (group_constraint_thresh_cmp_test.c:32-91), run through test_harness in a forked child. SKIP_IF(platform_check_for_tests()) returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99), reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0, before any event is opened. If have_hwcap2(PPC_FEATURE2_ARCH_3_1) it uses the power10 events: leader p10_EventCode_1 with attr.config1 = 1000 (event_open), then a sibling p10_EventCode_2 with config1 = 2000 whose event_open_with_group must fail (FAIL_IF(!...)), event_close of that sibling, then a new sibling p10_EventCode_2 with config1 = 1000 whose event_open_with_group must succeed, then it closes the leader and the sibling. Otherwise it uses the power9 events: leader p9_EventCode_1, sibling p9_EventCode_2 expected to fail, closed, then p9_EventCode_3 expected to succeed, then both closed. FAIL_IF prints a message and returns 1 at once: if the leader open fails nothing is open; if the mismatched open unexpectedly succeeds, the leader and that sibling are left open; if the matching open fails, the leader is left open. It returns 0 after the final closes (event_close results are not checked).
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose said failures of event_init/event_close are checked and the caller closes events) moot for the current text (the code does not check them and the test closes the events itself); round 2 and 15 (contract only bounds the result) moot, contract removed because the function uses structs and system calls. The old prose said SKIP_IF returns 0 and omitted the power10 branch; fixed (utils.h:160-167). Tally 0 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: main() of group_constraint_thresh_cmp_test.c (lines 93-96) returns test_harness(group_constraint_thresh_cmp, "group_constraint_thresh_cmp"). test_harness forks the test, waits for it with a timeout, and returns the test's exit status: 0 on pass, 0 when the test returned the skip value (the harness maps it to 0 after reporting the skip), 1 when the test function returned 1, and 1 for harness errors (fork or waitpid failure, killed by signal, timeout). The test function itself only returns 0, 1 or the skip value, so main returns 0 or 1.

Tally 0 right 1 wrong.

name: group_constraint_thresh_ctl
prose: Test function group_constraint_thresh_ctl() (group_constraint_thresh_ctl_test.c:31-59), run through test_harness in a forked child. If platform_check_for_tests() is nonzero, SKIP_IF returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99; reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) with no event opened. Otherwise it opens leader EventCode_1 with event_open and sibling EventCode_2 with event_open_with_group(&event, leader.fd), which is expected to fail; it then event_close()s that sibling, initialises EventCode_3 as a new sibling, expects event_open_with_group to succeed, and closes the leader and the sibling. The failure checks use FAIL_IF, which prints a message and returns 1 (not -1): when the leader's event_open fails nothing is open; when the mismatched sibling open unexpectedly succeeds, the leader and that sibling stay open; when the matching sibling open fails, the leader stays open. It returns 0 after the final closes (event_close results are not checked).
note: Reviewers: round 1 (returns 2 on skip and -1 on failure) wrong, the values are 99 and 1 (utils.h:119-126, 160-167; the old prose said 2 and -1); round 2 (contract omits cleanup) moot; round 15 (the leader-open failure path leaves no leader open) right (lines 39-40). Tally 1 right 1 wrong.

name: ptrace_tm_spd_tar
prose: Test function ptrace_tm_spd_tar() (ptrace-tm-spd-tar.c:126-166), run through test_harness in a forked child; TEST_PASS is 0 and TEST_FAIL is 1 (ptrace.h:33-34). It returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99; test_harness reports a skip with status 0) through SKIP_IF_MSG when !have_htm() or htm_is_synthetic(); the macro returns, it does not terminate the process, and 99 is not KSFT_SKIP. Otherwise it creates a 3-int SysV shared segment with shmget(IPC_PRIVATE, ..., 0777|IPC_CREAT) (the result is not checked) and forks. The child calls tm_spd_tar(), which ends in exit(0) or exit(1) and never returns. The parent attaches the segment as pptr with shmat (unchecked), sets pptr[0] and pptr[1] to 0 and spins until pptr[2] is nonzero (the child sets it in wait_parent); if fork() failed (pid == -1) the 'if (pid)' branch is still taken and the parent spins on pptr[2] with no child, so it never returns. It then calls trace_tm_spd_tar(pid). If that returns nonzero the parent sends SIGTERM to the child, calls shmdt(&pptr), shmctl(IPC_RMID) and returns TEST_FAIL. Otherwise it calls shmdt(&pptr), wait(&status), shmctl(IPC_RMID), returns TEST_FAIL if wait() did not return pid, and otherwise TEST_FAIL when the child exited normally with a nonzero status and TEST_PASS when it exited with status 0 or ended by a signal. Note shmdt(&pptr) passes the address of the pointer variable, not the attached address pptr, so it does not detach the segment (it fails; its result is ignored); shmctl(IPC_RMID) only marks the segment for removal.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (misstates TEST_FAIL causes; SKIP_IF_MSG exiting process) mixed: the skip macro returns 99 rather than exiting (utils.h:169-176) so the 'exiting' claim is wrong, while the old prose's KSFT_SKIP (4) was indeed wrong; round 2 (omits signaled-child path returning TEST_PASS) right (lines 162-163); round 15 (shmdt(&pptr) detaches the address of the local pointer, not the segment) right (lines 148, 153). Tally 2 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.

name: tm_vsx
prose: Function tm_vsx() (ptrace-tm-vsx.c:29-82) is the child side of the ptrace TM VSX test; it takes no parameters, uses the global shm_id, and never returns (every path ends in a loop or exit). It attaches the shared segment with cptr = shmat(shm_id, NULL, 0) (unchecked). At label trans it sets cptr[1] = 0 and runs an inline-asm block: it calls load_vsx_ckpt (loadvsx(fp_load_ckpt)) before the tbegin. instruction, i.e. outside the transaction, so the checkpointed VSX state is fp_load_ckpt; tbegin. then, inside the transaction, calls load_vsx (loads fp_load), tsuspends, stores the word 1 with stw to the address of cptr[1], tresumes, and then executes b . (an endless loop) which only ends when the transaction is aborted (the tend. after it is not reachable by normal flow). On the abort path the block sets result = 1 and reads TEXASR. After the block, if result is nonzero: if cptr[0] is still 0 it goes back to trans and retries; otherwise it calls shmdt(cptr), stores the VSX registers into fp_store with storevsx, and calls exit(1) if compare_vsx_vmx(fp_store, fp_load_ckpt_new) is nonzero and exit(0) if it is zero. If result is zero it detaches with shmdt(cptr) and calls exit(1). The parent is expected to set cptr[0] nonzero after writing new checkpointed VSX/VMX state through ptrace.
note: Reviewers: original (precondition omits that cptr[0] must be set; code loops when unset) right (lines 69-71); round 2 (code attaches via shmat and retries while cptr[0] is zero) right; round 15 (load_vsx_ckpt runs before tbegin, outside the transaction) right (lines 39-43). All three were against earlier wording; the text is rewritten from the code. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: uaccess_flush_test
prose: Test function uaccess_flush_test() (uaccess_flush.c:21-153), run through test_harness in a forked child. SKIP_IF and FAIL_IF are macros that return MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99, reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) or 1 from the function; they do not terminate the process. It returns 99 when geteuid() != 0, when the CPU lacks PPC_FEATURE_ARCH_2_06, or when reading any of the debugfs files powerpc/rfi_flush, powerpc/entry_flush or powerpc/uaccess_flush fails (after perror). It then writes 0 to rfi_flush and entry_flush when their original values were nonzero (a write failure returns 1), opens an L1D read-miss perf counter (fd < 0 returns 1), allocates a buffer with memalign (its arguments are alignment zero_size and size CACHELINE_SIZE; the result is not checked or freed), enables the counter (failure returns 1) and calls set_dscr(1). It then measures in two rounds of 10 repetitions each: round one with uaccess_flush equal to its original value, round two after writing the opposite value (!uaccess_flush_orig) to powerpc/uaccess_flush (a write failure returns 1 without restoring anything). Each repetition resets the counter (failure returns 1), runs syscall_loop_uaccess(p, 100000, 24 KiB), reads the counter (a short read returns 1) and counts a pass when uaccess_flush is nonzero and L1D misses >= iterations * (zero_size / CACHELINE_SIZE - 2), or when it is zero and misses are below half that. After each round it prints PASS or FAIL and sets rc = 1 if passes < repetitions (rc is never reset). After the second round it disables and closes the counter, sets DSCR to 0, and restores rfi_flush, entry_flush and uaccess_flush to their original values, returning 1 at the first restore write that fails (so earlier restores have happened, later ones not), and finally returns rc (0 or 1). The early returns 1 taken after the counter was opened and before it is closed (failures of enable, reset, read, and of the uaccess_flush write) leave the perf counter open, DSCR at 1 once set_dscr(1) has run, and rfi_flush/entry_flush at 0 if they were changed; the failure return after perf_event_open (fd < 0) also leaves rfi_flush/entry_flush at 0 if they were changed; the restore-failure returns happen after the counter is closed.
note: Reviewers: original (returns 1 on debugfs write failures without restoring original values; omits writability) right (lines 54-66, 122-125); round 15 (restore-failure returns after the second round occur after perf_event_disable/close, so the counter is not open) right (lines 132-150). The old prose also said SKIP_IF/FAIL_IF terminate the process, which is wrong (they return). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of testptp.c (lines 156-694; the slice showed only the middle). It parses options with getopt using "cd:e:E:f:F:ghH:i:k:lL:n:o:p:P:rsSt:T:w:x:Xy:z" and stores the settings; it does not run anything until parsing is complete. During parsing it returns -1 (after usage or a message) when -L does not parse as "pin,func" (usage), when -x is outside 1..PTP_MAX_SAMPLES, when -y is not realtime, monotonic or monotonic-raw, and for an unknown option or '?'; -h prints usage and returns 0 immediately, without opening the device. It then opens the device (default DEVICE, read-only when -r, else read-write); an open failure prints a message and returns -1 (nothing to close). get_clockid failing returns -1 with fd left open. It then performs the requested operations in a fixed order, reporting per-operation errors with perror and continuing: -c capabilities, -f frequency adjust, -t/-n time shift, -o phase adjust, -g get time, -s/-S/-T set time, -L pin function, -e external timestamps (reads events, and disables the request afterwards unless -r), -z flag test, -l pin listing, then checks that -w and -H are used only together with -p (else prints a message and returns -1 with fd open), -p periodic output (a clock_gettime failure returns -1 with fd open), -P PPS, -k system/phc offset samples (n_samples outside 1..25 prints usage and returns -1 with fd open; calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), -x extended timestamps (calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), -X cross timestamp (calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), and -F channel masking (clears the mask, enables one channel and waits for getchar()). Operations already done before a -1 return are not undone. When it reaches the end it closes fd and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (omits -h returning 0 without opening the device; 'fd left open' is false when the open fails) right on both (testptp.c:313-315, 323-327). Old prose also said the -k count check is part of option parsing; it happens after the earlier operations have run (lines 553-558). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: run_single_test
prose: Static function run_single_test(test, uparams) in resctrl_tests.c (lines 119-156); it returns nothing. If test->disabled is set it returns at once without printing anything. If the vendor check fails (test_vendor_specific_check, true when the test has no vendor_specific mask or get_vendor() matches it) it calls ksft_test_result_skip and returns. It then reads snc_mode = snc_nodes_per_l3_cache() and prints "Starting <name> test ..."; if snc_mode == 1 and snc_unreliable is set and get_vendor() == ARCH_INTEL it reports a skip (SNC detection unreliable) and returns. Then test_prepare(test) (signal handler registration and mounting resctrl; it unregisters the handler itself if the mount fails) failing calls ksft_exit_fail_msg, which ends the process; the 'return' after it is not reached. If test->feature_check(test) is false it reports a skip and goes to cleanup. Otherwise it runs test->run_test(test, uparams) and reports ksft_test_result(!ret, ...), pass when the return value is 0. The cleanup path, reached after a feature-check skip or after a reported result, runs test_cleanup: it calls test->cleanup if that is set, umount_resctrlfs() and signal_handler_unregister().
note: Reviewers: original (disabled tests return silently without skip message; the feature-check skip is not pass/fail) right (lines 123-124, 145-149); round 15 (SNC skip also requires snc_mode == 1) right (line 135). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(map, data_mmap)
prose: Test body (map_test.c:214-261; the slice began at line 255 inside it, so no test named metadata_pages_protection exists) for the map fixture, whose setup maps the per-CPU ring buffer of the current CPU into self->map_desc (desc->meta, desc->cpu_fd). It computes meta_len = meta_page_size and data_len = subbuf_size * nr_subbufs and, with ASSERT_*, checks that mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, cpu_fd, offset meta_len) succeeds for the whole data area and for data_len - subbuf_size (each unmapped again); that mapping data_len (minus one subbuf) at offset meta_len + 2 * subbuf_size fails with MAP_FAILED (size overflow); and that mapping the full data_len at offset data_len + 2 * subbuf_size fails with MAP_FAILED (offset outside the buffer). If meta_page_size is larger than getpagesize() it maps the meta page area at offset 0 (must succeed), checks with ASSERT_EQ that every int from offset meta_struct_len up to meta_page_size reads as 0 (padding), and unmaps it. The body returns nothing; the first failed ASSERT ends it.
note: Old record was dropped (name 'metadata_pages_protection' is not in the source). The slice was the tail of TEST_F(map, data_mmap) (map_test.c:214), so it is fixed under that real name.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of param_test.c (lines 1483-1660; the slice was the tail). It scans argv from index 1, ignoring arguments that do not start with '-'. For -1 to -9 it needs a following argument (otherwise usage and return -1) and stores atol of it in loop_cnt[digit]; -m, -s, -D, -t and -r also need a following argument and a non-negative value (else usage and return -1) and set opt_modulo, opt_sleep, opt_disable_mod, opt_threads, opt_reps; -y, -k, -d, -v and -M set flags (opt_yield, opt_signal, opt_disable_rseq, verbose, opt_mo = RSEQ_MO_RELEASE); -T needs an argument whose first character is one of s, l, i, b, m, r (opt_test is set to it; any other character gives usage and return -1; opt_test defaults to 's'); -h prints usage and returns 0 at once (goto end); any other option gives usage and returns -1. After parsing it copies loop_cnt[1..6] to loop_cnt_1..6 and calls set_signal_handler (nonzero returns -1). Unless -d was given it registers the thread with rseq_register_current_thread (nonzero returns -1) and requires rseq_validate_cpu_id() (otherwise prints 'cpu id getter unavailable' and returns -1). It then runs exactly one test selected by opt_test: s spinlock, l linked list, b buffer, m memcpy buffer, i counter increment, r membarrier. Unless -d was given it calls rseq_unregister_current_thread and calls abort() if that is nonzero. It returns 0 at the end.
note: Reviewer round 15 (an unknown opt_test falls through the switch and returns 0; no default error path) wrong: -T rejects any selector other than the six letters during parsing (param_test.c:1585-1596) and opt_test starts as 's' (line 40), so the final switch always matches a case. The old prose's 'running the selected test (if any)' was loose: one test always runs, spinlock by default. Tally 0 right 1 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of cs_prctl_test.c (lines 232-359; the slice began inside it). Globals: num_processes defaults to 2 and the local num_threads to 3, delay to 0. getopt uses ":hkT:P:d:": -P and -T set the process and thread counts (strtol/strtoul, no error check), -d the delay, -k sets keypress (and later delay = -1), -h calls printf(USAGE) and exit(EXIT_SUCCESS); any other result, including a missing option argument, calls handle_usage(20, "unknown option") which exits with status 20. num_processes outside 1..MAX_PROCESSES exits through handle_usage(1, ...), num_threads outside 1..MAX_THREADS through handle_usage(2, ...). It seeds rand with time, puts itself in a new process group with setpgid(0, 0) (failure calls handle_error, which exits with EXIT_FAILURE), creates num_processes child processes each with num_threads threads (a pipe failure calls handle_error; clone failures of the processes are not checked), sets need_cleanup, and runs a fixed sequence of core-scheduling prctl calls with validate() checks of the cookies (PR_SCHED_CORE_CREATE on the process group, CREATE on a random child's TGID, SHARE_TO that pid, SHARE_FROM one of its threads, SHARE_TO the process group). Each of these five _prctl calls returning < 0 calls handle_error (which prints, SIGTERMs all children if need_cleanup is set, and exits EXIT_FAILURE). Two further _prctl calls (PR_SCHED_CORE_MAX, and SHARE_TO with a nonzero arg5) are expected to fail with EINVAL and are checked through validate(), not handle_error. validate() counts failures in errors. After the sequence it prints TESTS FAILED with the error count and sets res = 10 when errors is nonzero, else prints SUCCESS. It then waits for getchar() when -k was given, otherwise sleeps delay seconds, sends signal 15 to each child process, and returns res (0 or 10).
note: Reviewer round 15 (the two expected-EINVAL _prctl calls are validated, not passed to handle_error) right (cs_prctl_test.c:337-341). The old prose also said both counts default to 3; num_processes defaults to 2 (line 74). Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: exit_from_hotplug
prose: Static function exit_from_hotplug(cpu, onlining) in hotplug.bpf.c (lines 20-35), a BPF helper that returns nothing, called by hotplug_cpu_online (onlining = true) and hotplug_cpu_offline (onlining = false). It first calls scx_bpf_create_dsq(0, -1) and ignores the result (the comment says this only verifies that blocking kfuncs can be called from the hotplug path; the arguments are the DSQ id 0 and a NUMA node of -1, not a priority). It then computes code = SCX_ECODE_ACT_RESTART | HOTPLUG_EXIT_RSN, ORs in HOTPLUG_ONLINING when onlining is true, and calls scx_bpf_exit(code, "hotplug event detected (%d going %s)", cpu, "online" or "offline"), which requests that the sched_ext scheduler exit with that code and message. Nothing follows that call in this function.
note: Reviewers: original (omits the scx_bpf_create_dsq side effect) right (hotplug.bpf.c:26); round 15 (second argument of scx_bpf_create_dsq is the NUMA node, not a priority) right (the old prose said priority -1; the file comment and signature show a node argument). The old claim that scx_bpf_exit does not return is not shown by this file, so it was removed. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F_SIGNAL(precedence, kill_is_highest, SIGSYS)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1280-1307) for the precedence fixture, whose setup allocates six filter programs (allow, log, trace, error, trap, kill). Each program loads the syscall number and returns SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW for every syscall except getpid, for which it returns its own action (allow: always allow). The body reads getppid, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (ASSERT_EQ 0), and installs, with prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER) and ASSERT_EQ(0, ...) each, the filters in the order allow, log, trace, error, trap, kill. It then expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to equal the parent pid (EXPECT_EQ) and calls syscall(__NR_getpid) with the comment 'should never return': the kill filter has the highest precedence, so the process is expected to be killed with SIGSYS, which is what TEST_F_SIGNAL(..., SIGSYS) checks. The final EXPECT_EQ(0, res) is only reached if getpid returns, which would be a failure.
note: Generated name replaced by the real macro invocation. Old prose checked against seccomp_bpf.c:1179-1307; it was essentially right but called the death 'the call never returns' without stating that SIGSYS death is the expected outcome checked by the TEST_F_SIGNAL harness. No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F_SIGNAL(precedence, trap_is_second, SIGSYS)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1336-1359) for the precedence fixture (six per-action filters that allow everything except getpid, for which they return their action). It reads getppid, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs the filters allow, log, trace, error, trap in that order (each prctl asserted 0). It expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to return the parent pid and then calls syscall(__NR_getpid): the trap filter has the highest precedence among those installed, so the kernel raises SIGSYS; the test installs no handler, so the process is expected to die from SIGSYS, which TEST_F_SIGNAL(..., SIGSYS) checks. The last EXPECT_EQ(0, ...) is only reached if getpid returned.
note: Real macro invocation used. No reviewer claim; old prose said 'caught by the trap filter so the process dies with SIGSYS', which is right in effect (no handler installed in this test).

name: TEST_F(precedence, errno_is_third)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1386-1406) for the precedence fixture. It reads getppid, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs the filters allow, log, trace, error in that order (each prctl asserted 0). It then expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to equal the parent pid and syscall(__NR_getpid) to return 0: the error filter's SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO has errno data 0, so the call fails with errno 0 and returns 0 in the test's view, and it wins over the log and trace actions. Both are non-fatal EXPECT_EQ checks.
note: Real macro invocation used. Prior prose checked against the code; the 'returns 0' claim is from the expectation at line 1405. No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(precedence, trace_is_fourth)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1430-1449) for the precedence fixture. It reads getppid, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs the filters allow, log, trace in that order (each prctl asserted 0). It expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to equal the parent pid and, under the comment 'No ptracer', syscall(__NR_getpid) to return -1: the trace filter's SECCOMP_RET_TRACE with no tracer attached makes the call fail, and it takes precedence over the log filter. Both are non-fatal EXPECT_EQ checks; the test does not set errno expectations.
note: Real macro invocation used. The ENOSYS reason in the old prose is not shown by this file (only the comment 'No ptracer' and the expected -1), so it is dropped. No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(precedence, log_is_fifth)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1472-1490) for the precedence fixture. It records mypid = getpid() and parent = getppid() before installing anything, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS and installs the filters allow and log (each prctl asserted 0). It then expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to equal parent and syscall(__NR_getpid) to equal mypid: the log filter returns SECCOMP_RET_LOG for getpid, which lets the call proceed (and be logged). Both are non-fatal EXPECT_EQ checks.
note: Real macro invocation used. No reviewer claim; prior prose checked.

name: TEST_F(TRACE_syscall, syscall_allowed)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:2224-2229) for the TRACE_syscall fixture, which runs in two variants. In the ptrace variant a tracer (tracer_ptrace) watches the process with PTRACE_SYSCALL and no seccomp filter is installed; in the seccomp variant a filter returns SECCOMP_RET_TRACE|0x1005 for getppid (and trace actions for getpid, gettid and openat), and tracer_seccomp does nothing for 0x1005. The body checks with non-fatal EXPECT macros that syscall(__NR_getppid) returns self->parent and that it is different from self->mypid. A failed expectation is recorded and the body continues; nothing is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT_* do not abort; the getppid filter returns TRACE, not ALLOW) right on both (seccomp_bpf.c:2154-2155, 2227-2228, 2037-2039). The old prose said the fixture allows the call and that a mismatch aborts. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(TRACE_syscall, syscall_redirected)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:2231-2236) for the TRACE_syscall fixture. The fixture's tracer rewrites getpid to getppid: in the ptrace variant tracer_ptrace sets the syscall number to __NR_getppid at entry or exit as the architecture allows (lines 2103-2108), in the seccomp variant the filter returns SECCOMP_RET_TRACE|0x1002 for getpid and tracer_seccomp changes the syscall number to __NR_getppid (lines 2022-2026). The body checks with non-fatal EXPECT macros that syscall(__NR_getpid) returns self->parent and differs from self->mypid. A failed expectation does not abort; nothing is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT_* do not abort the test) right (lines 2234-2235). The old prose said a mismatch aborts. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: user_notif_syscall
prose: Static function user_notif_syscall(nr, flags) in seccomp_bpf.c (lines 3360-3376). It builds a four-instruction classic BPF filter on the stack that loads the syscall number and returns SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF when it equals nr and SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW otherwise, and returns the result of seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER, flags, &prog), where seccomp() sets errno to 0 and returns syscall(__NR_seccomp, ...). So it returns what the kernel returns: 0 on success; with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER in flags, the new notification listener file descriptor (non-negative) on success; and -1 with errno set by the kernel on failure (the errors depend on the kernel, for example EINVAL for unsupported flags or EACCES without no_new_privs or CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and are not produced by this code); a SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC failure can return a positive thread id. The filter is installed for the calling thread (and, with TSYNC, its threads) and stays installed for the process lifetime; the stack filter array is copied by the kernel.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (EFAULT cannot occur because the filter pointer is a valid local array) right; round 15 (success can return a listener fd when flags include SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER, not always 0) right (seccomp_bpf.c:305-309, 3360-3375, callers at 3423). The old prose also enumerated errno values the code does not produce. The TSYNC return value is from the seccomp(2) interface, not from this file. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST(user_notification_continue)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:3842-3926). It sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (ASSERT_EQ 0), installs a user-notification filter for __NR_dup with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER through user_notif_syscall (ASSERT_GE 0 for the listener), and forks (ASSERT_GE 0). The child creates a pipe, calls dup on the read end (which is held for the supervisor), asserts the fd differs, and ASSERT_EQ(filecmp(self, self, pipe_fds[0], dup_fd), 0) before exit(0). The parent polls the listener (expecting revents == POLLIN), receives the notification with SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_RECV (expecting 0), polls again (expecting revents == POLLOUT), expects req.data.nr == __NR_dup, and sets resp.id and resp.flags = SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE. It then sends SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SEND three times: with error 0 and val USER_NOTIF_MAGIC it expects -1 with errno EINVAL, with error USER_NOTIF_MAGIC and val 0 the same, and with error 0 and val 0 it expects 0 (if that fails with EINVAL the SKIP(goto skip, ...) jumps to the reap step). It finally expects waitpid to return the child's pid, the child to have exited normally, and its exit status to be 0; a status of 2 makes the test skip with SKIP(return, ...) (kcmp not supported). Everything uses non-fatal EXPECT_* except the ASSERTs named above; nothing is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT macros do not abort; they record failure and continue) right (seccomp_bpf.c:3880-3925). Also the old prose said it returns early when the send fails with EINVAL; the code jumps to the waitpid step instead (line 3914, 3917). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(enclave, clobbered_vdso)
prose: Test body (sgx/main.c:504-530) for the enclave fixture. It requires setup_test_encl(ENCL_HEAP_SIZE_DEFAULT, &self->encl, _metadata) to return true (ASSERT_TRUE, which ends the test on failure), zeroes self->run and sets run.tcs to the enclave base. It then calls ENCL_CALL(op, run, true), i.e. vdso_sgx_enter_enclave with EENTER, first with an ENCL_OP_PUT_TO_BUFFER operation (value MAGIC) and then with ENCL_OP_GET_FROM_BUFFER (value initialised to 0), expecting each call to return 0, EXPECT_EEXIT(&run) (run.function == EEXIT), run.user_data == 0, and for the get operation get_op.value == MAGIC. Apart from the setup ASSERT these are non-fatal EXPECT checks: a mismatch is recorded and the test continues.
note: Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT_EQ/EXPECT_EEXIT are non-fatal, mismatches fail but do not abort) right (sgx/main.c:274-280, 517-529). The old prose said 'aborting on any mismatch'. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(enclave, pte_permissions)
prose: Test body (sgx/main.c:616-715) for the enclave fixture. After ASSERT_TRUE(setup_test_encl(...)) and zeroing self->run, it takes data_start = encl_base + data offset + PAGE_SIZE (the second page of the .data segment). It writes MAGIC to data_start with ENCL_OP_PUT_TO_ADDRESS and reads it back with ENCL_OP_GET_FROM_ADDRESS, expecting call result 0, EEXIT, zero exception fields and value MAGIC. It then mprotect()s the page to PROT_READ (a failure only prints with perror), sets the put value to MAGIC2 and calls the enclave again, expecting the call to return 0 with exception_vector 14, exception_error_code 0x7 and exception_addr == data_start (a page fault reported through the vDSO); it clears the three exception fields, mprotect()s the page back to PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE (failure only perror), resumes the enclave with vdso_sgx_enter_enclave(..., ERESUME, ...) expecting 0, EEXIT and no exception, and finally reads the address again expecting MAGIC2, EEXIT and no exception. All of these are non-fatal EXPECT checks; only the setup assertion ends the test.
note: Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT_* are non-fatal) right. The old prose also said a faulting write was checked with 'no mismatch aborts'. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: test4_lseek
prose: Static function test4_lseek(fd) in adi-test.c (lines 466-513). It checks a sequence of seeks on the ADI device descriptor using seek_adi, which calls lseek(fd, offset, whence), records the timing on success, and then always calls lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) with the result ignored before returning the result of the first lseek; the test does not assume that this extra call moves the position (it expects the following SEEK_CUR calls to continue from the previous offset). Steps: (1) seek_adi(fd, 0x123456789abcdef0, SEEK_SET) must return the same offset, else ret = -1; (2) the same SEEK_SET again must return a negative value with errno == EINVAL, else ret = -2 (errno is read after seek_adi's extra lseek, which could change it); (3) seek_adi(fd, 0, SEEK_CUR) must return the original offset, else -3; (4) seek_adi(fd, 0x100, SEEK_CUR) must return offset + 0x100, else -4; (5) seek_adi(fd, 0xFFFFFFF000000000, SEEK_CUR) must return offset + 0x100 + 0xFFFFFFF000000000, else -5. A failing step prints a message with the step code to stderr and jumps to out; with all steps passing ret = 0. It returns ret (through RETURN_FROM_TEST, which may print a debug line). The fd stays open and nothing is allocated.
note: Reviewer round 15 (seek_adi does not leave fd at EOF: the SEEK_END result is ignored and the test expects the position unchanged) right (adi-test.c:308-310, 492-508); the old prose claimed each seek_adi leaves fd at end-of-file. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: change_skew_test
prose: Function change_skew_test(ppm) in change_skew.c (lines 33-52). It declares an uninitialised struct timex, sets only modes = ADJ_FREQUENCY and freq = ppm << 16, and calls adjtimex. The shift is defined only for 0 <= ppm <= 32767 (a negative ppm shifts a negative value, and ppm >= 32768 overflows int); the function does not check ppm. If adjtimex returns a negative value it prints "Error adjusting freq" and returns that value without running the child programs. Otherwise it runs system("./raw_skew"), system("./inconsistency-check") and system("./nanosleep") in that order and returns the bitwise OR of the three system() results (the adjtimex result is not part of it): each is -1 if the child could not be run or the wait status otherwise, so the result is -1 if any of them failed to start, else 0 only when all three exited with status 0, and otherwise nonzero.
note: No reviewer claims on the current text (round 2 claim on negative ppm is already in the text). Checked against change_skew.c:33-52.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of change_skew.c (lines 55-93); argc and argv are unused. It first runs system("killall -9 ntpd") (result ignored), then calls adjtimex with modes = ADJ_OFFSET and offset = 0 on an uninitialised struct timex; the call's copy-back fills the whole struct from the kernel, including tx.freq. If that call returns a negative value it prints "Maybe you're not running as root?" and returns -1. Otherwise it loops over ppm values 0, 250, 500, -250, -500, printing "Using %i ppm adjustment" and calling change_skew_test(ppm), and stops at the first nonzero result (which includes a negative adjtimex result inside change_skew_test). It then calls adjtimex with modes = ADJ_FREQUENCY and tx.offset = 0 (ignored, since ADJ_OFFSET is not in modes) with tx.freq still equal to the value copied back by the first adjtimex call, so the frequency is set back to that earlier value; its return value is ignored. Finally, if the last result was nonzero it prints "[FAIL]" and calls ksft_exit_fail(); otherwise it prints "[OK]" and calls ksft_exit_pass(). Both exit the process, so main does not return normally after the first adjtimex succeeds.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (claims it resets frequency but leaves tx.freq uninitialised) wrong, tx.freq holds the value copied back by the first adjtimex (change_skew.c:66-68, 83-85); round 2 (tx.freq is set by the earlier copy-back, not uninitialised) right. Tally 1 right 1 wrong. The old prose omitted the killall call.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of leap-a-day.c (lines 178-381; the slice began inside it). getopt uses "wti:": -w sets settime = 0 and prints a message, -i sets the iteration count (atoi, default 10), -t enables TAI output; any other option prints usage and calls exit(-1). With -t it checks clock_gettime(CLOCK_TAI): on failure it prints a message and calls ksft_exit_fail(). It installs handler for SIGINT (and tries SIGKILL, which cannot be caught) and sigalarm as the handler for SIGRTMAX; handler calls clear_time_state() and exit(0). Each loop iteration computes next_leap as the next UTC midnight, sets the system time to next_leap - 10 seconds unless -w was given, calls clear_time_state(), sets STA_INS (or STA_DEL, alternating each iteration through insert) with adjtimex, and checks it was set. adjtimex returning negative, the flag not being set, and timer_create failing each print a message and call ksft_exit_fail() without calling clear_time_state(). It arms a timer for next_leap, sleeps until 3 seconds before it, re-sets the flag if it was cleared, and prints adjtimex state every half second until the reported time reaches next_leap + 2. It then flips insert, runs test_hrtimer_failure, and if error_found is set (by sigalarm or test_hrtimer_failure) it prints a message, calls clear_time_state() and ksft_exit_fail(). The loop ends with 'if iterations != -1 and --iterations == 0 break', so iterations -1 loops until interrupted, and values 0 or below -1 also never reach zero. After the loop it calls clear_time_state() and ksft_exit_pass(). Since ksft_exit_* terminate the process, main does not return to its caller.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the adjtimex and timer_create failure paths call ksft_exit_fail() without clear_time_state(), contradicting 'before exiting it clears') right (leap-a-day.c:271-275, 280-284, 299-302). The old prose also missed that the CLOCK_TAI failure exit and the usage exit(-1) differ from the clear_time_state paths. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: loop_queue_tgt_io
prose: Static function loop_queue_tgt_io(t, q, tag) in ublk/file_backed.c (lines 77-103) takes a ublk thread, a queue and a tag; it fetches the I/O descriptor with ublk_get_iod(q, tag). It dispatches on ublksrv_get_op(iod): UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH calls loop_queue_flush_io, which allocates one SQE with ublk_io_alloc_sqes (not checked for failure), prepares an IORING_FSYNC_DATASYNC fsync on the registered backing file with IOSQE_FIXED_FILE and returns 1; UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE_ZEROES and UBLK_IO_OP_DISCARD give -ENOTSUP without preparing any SQE; UBLK_IO_OP_READ and UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE call loop_queue_tgt_rw_io; any other operation gives -EINVAL. loop_queue_tgt_rw_io has two shapes: when the queue is not zero-copy or uses auto zero-copy it allocates one SQE and returns -ENOMEM if the SQE pointer is NULL, otherwise prepares one read/write SQE and returns 1; when it is zero-copy without auto zero-copy it allocates three SQEs (not checked), prepares a buffer-register, a fixed read/write and a buffer-unregister SQE and returns 2. So the return value is 1 (flush, or one-SQE read/write), 2 (three-SQE zero-copy read/write), -ENOTSUP, -EINVAL, or -ENOMEM (only from the one-SQE read/write path). A debug message is logged on every path before returning.
note: Reviewers: original (omits -ENOMEM) right; round 15 (-ENOMEM is only checked in the non-zc read/write path; zero-copy and flush SQE allocations are unchecked) right (file_backed.c:22, 40-43, 57-59). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: trigger_uevent
prose: Function trigger_uevent(times) in uevent_filtering.c (lines 195-218) opens "/sys/devices/virtual/mem/full/uevent" with O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC. If the open fails it returns -1 when errno is ENOENT and -EINVAL for any other errno. Otherwise it loops i from 0 to times - 1, writing the 4 bytes "add\n" with write_nointr (which retries on EINTR and returns write()'s result: the byte count, or -1 with errno set on failure); on a negative result it prints "Failed to trigger uevent" and stops the loop. It closes the fd and returns ret, the result of the last write performed: 4 when the writes succeeded (a short write would return its smaller count), or -1 when the last write failed (the value is -1, not a negative errno). If times is 0, ret is never assigned and the returned value is indeterminate.
note: Reviewers: original (positive write count; prose swaps open errors) right on the first part (the old text already fixed the open errors); round 2 (open error mapping: ENOENT gives -1, other errors -EINVAL) right (uevent_filtering.c:201-206), the old text had it correct; round 15 (a failed write returns -1, not a negative errno) right (lines 209-217, write_nointr at 42-50). Contract removed because the function does file I/O. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: mess_with_syscall
prose: Static function mess_with_syscall(testpid, pass) in x86/syscall_numbering.c (lines 353-395); returns nothing. It first sets sh->probing_syscall = false. For pass PTP_NOTHING or PTP_DONE it returns at once without touching the child's registers. Otherwise it reads the child's registers with PTRACE_GETREGS (the result is not checked) and, if regs.orig_rax differs from regs.rbx, calls fail(), which prints a message and increments sh->nerr but does not stop. Then by pass: PTP_GETREGS returns without writing registers; PTP_WRITEBACK writes them back unchanged; PTP_FUZZRET sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE (-9999); PTP_FUZZHIGH sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE and ORs 0xffffffff00000000 into orig_rax; PTP_INTNUM sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE and replaces orig_rax with (int)orig_rax (sign extension of the low 32 bits). For these three and PTP_WRITEBACK it then calls PTRACE_SETREGS (result not checked). For any other pass value (not reachable with the enum values handled above) it calls crit(), which prints a failure and a skip message and calls exit(EX_OSERR), so PTRACE_SETREGS is not reached.
note: Reviewers: original (PTP_GETREGS returns without PTRACE_SETREGS; PTP_NOTHING/DONE still clear probing_syscall) right (syscall_numbering.c:357-374); round 2 and round 15 (crit does not return, so the default path does not write registers back) right (lines 99-105, 389-391). The old prose said the default path writes the unchanged registers back, which is wrong. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of x86/test_shadow_stack.c in the build variant that has CET support (lines 978-1087; when the compiler is older than GCC 8.5 a different main at line 64 just prints a skip message and returns 0). argc and argv are unused; ret starts at 0. It enables the shadow stack with ARCH_PRCTL(ARCH_SHSTK_ENABLE, ARCH_SHSTK_SHSTK); failure prints "[SKIP] Could not enable Shadow stack" and returns 1. It disables it again (failure prints a [FAIL] message and sets ret = 1 but continues), then re-enables it (failure prints a [SKIP] message and returns 1, leaving the shadow stack in whatever state it is). It enables WRSS with ARCH_SHSTK_WRSS: failure prints a [SKIP] message, sets ret = 1 and jumps to the out label. If get_ssp() returns 0 it prints "[FAIL] Shadow stack disabled" and returns 1 directly. It then runs, in order, test_shstk_pivot, test_shstk_faults, test_shstk_violation, test_gup, test_mprotect, test_userfaultfd, test_guard_gap_other_gaps, test_guard_gap_new_mappings_gaps, test_ptrace, test_32bit, test_uretprobe; for each nonzero result it sets ret = 1 and prints a [FAIL] message, and goes to out at once, except for test_ptrace, which only prints and sets ret and lets the following tests run. If it gets through all tests it executes 'return ret' directly (line 1074), without disabling the shadow stack; the out label, reached only from the failure jumps, disables the shadow stack with ARCH_SHSTK_DISABLE (failure prints [FAIL] and sets ret = 1) and then returns ret. So ret is 1 on any recorded failure and 0 otherwise.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the normal path returns ret before the out label, so it does not disable the shadow stack) right (test_shadow_stack.c:1074-1086); the old prose said disabling happens on both paths. The old text also did not mention the alternate main at line 64. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: enable_tracer
prose: Static function enable_tracer() in latency-collector.c (lines 1437-1446), no parameters, no return value. It is meant to run after save_and_disable_tracer() has filled save_state (the saved option values, their valid flags and the saved threshold string). It takes save_state.mutex, calls set_trace_opts(&save_state, use_options), then write_file(TR_THRESH, save_state.thresh, threshold, ERR_CLEANUP) and write_file(TR_CURRENT, NOP_TRACER, current_tracer, ERR_CLEANUP), and releases the mutex. set_trace_opts writes to the trace_options file, through set_trace_opt, each option that was found to exist (opt_valid) and whose saved value differs from the wanted use_options value, warning and calling cleanup_exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if a write fails. write_file writes the global string threshold (not the saved threshold) to the threshold file, skipped when the saved value is non-NULL and equal to it (needs_change), and writes the global current_tracer to the current_tracer file, skipped when it equals "nop" (NOP_TRACER); a failed write warns with warnx and calls cleanup_exit(EXIT_FAILURE) (ERR_CLEANUP). Verbose messages are printed under print_mtx after successful writes. The saved tracer name is not used. A write failure does not return, since cleanup_exit exits the process.
note: Reviewers: original (writes use_options/threshold/current_tracer, not saved state; saved tracer unused) right; round 15 (it writes the global threshold, not save_state.thresh, to TR_THRESH) right (latency-collector.c:1442; save_state.thresh is only the comparison value). The old prose described writing save_state.thresh. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: timerlat_aa_init
prose: Function timerlat_aa_init(tool, dump_tasks) in rtla/src/timerlat_aa.c (lines 1023-1056). It reads nr_cpus locally with sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF), allocates a zeroed timerlat_aa_context (failure returns -1 with nothing installed), stores it in the global __timerlat_aa_ctx (overwriting any previous pointer without freeing it) and fills nr_cpus, tool and dump_tasks. It then allocates the per-CPU taa_data array with calloc(nr_cpus, ...), calls timerlat_aa_init_seqs(taa_ctx) and timerlat_aa_register_events(tool, dump_tasks). If any of those three fails it calls timerlat_aa_destroy() and returns -1; timerlat_aa_destroy frees the context (and, when taa_data was allocated, first unregisters the events, destroys the seqs and frees taa_data) but does not reset __timerlat_aa_ctx, so the global is left pointing at freed memory after a failed init. On success it returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (prose claims nr_cpus = sysconf(...) but code uses a caller-supplied nr_cpus parameter) wrong: nr_cpus is a local initialised from sysconf (timerlat_aa.c:1025) and there is no such parameter. The old text's allocation-failure paths were right; the dangling-global detail is new (timerlat_aa.c:1001-1016, 1033). Tally 0 right 1 wrong.

name: timerlat_bpf_wait
prose: Function timerlat_bpf_wait(timeout) in rtla/src/timerlat_bpf.c (lines 96-107), compiled only with HAVE_BPF_SKEL. It uses the file-scope skeleton pointer bpf, which must already have been loaded by timerlat_bpf_init (there is no NULL check). It creates a libbpf ring buffer on the signal_stop_tracing map with ring_buffer__new(bpf_map__fd(...), handle_rb_event, NULL, NULL), where handle_rb_event ignores the data and returns 0, then calls ring_buffer__poll(rb, timeout * 1000), frees the ring buffer with ring_buffer__free and returns the poll result. The result of ring_buffer__new is not checked: if it returned NULL, ring_buffer__poll would dereference it (libbpf's ring_buffer__poll reads rb->epoll_fd without a NULL check), so there is no -EINVAL return for a failed creation. ring_buffer__poll returns the number of records consumed (capped at INT_MAX, 0 on timeout), or a negative errno taken from epoll_wait (for example -EINTR when a signal interrupts the wait) or from record processing. The argument is multiplied by 1000 before being passed as the millisecond timeout, so timeout is in units of 1000 ms, and a negative value makes epoll_wait wait without a timeout; the int multiplication overflows for |timeout| above 2147483.
note: Old record was still-rejected on mechanical contract-vs-prose checks only (no reviewer claim). I checked libbpf's ring_buffer__poll and ring_buffer__free in tools/lib/bpf/ringbuf.c:172-187, 336-357. The old claims that a ring-buffer creation failure returns -EINVAL and that the free means 'no reference escapes' were unsupported or wrong, and the contract is dropped because the function uses the global bpf and system calls.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of aio_multibuff.c (lines 234-380; the slice began at 256). It returns 1 after printing a message when argc != 2 and when the malloc of ep_path fails. It builds "<argv[1]>/ep0", opens it O_RDWR and writes the descriptors and then the strings structures to it; an open failure or a write returning < 0 prints with perror and returns 1 (ep_path and, once opened, ep0 are not released). It opens "<argv[1]>/ep1" (failure returns 1 without freeing ep_path or closing ep0) and then frees ep_path. After that point it zeroes ctx and calls io_setup(AIO_MAX, &ctx), and eventfd(0, 0); a failure of either prints a message and returns 1 (ep0 and ep1, and after the eventfd failure also the aio context, are not released; ep_path is already freed). It then initialises two io_buffer sets with init_bufs and loops on select over ep0 and the eventfd: select failing with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries) breaks the loop; ep0 events go to handle_ep0, which sets the 'ready' flag; until ready is true the loop continues; for each of the two buffer sets that has no requests outstanding it prepares pwrite requests on ep1 with eventfd notification and submits them with io_submit, recording the number accepted (a failed io_submit is only printed); when the eventfd is readable it reads it (a failed read breaks the loop), reaps events with io_getevents(ctx, 1, BUFS_MAX, ...), subtracts them from the current buffer's outstanding count and advances to the other buffer when the count is 0. After a break it deletes both buffer sets with delete_bufs, io_destroy(ctx), closes ep1 and ep0 and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (the prose says the allocated path is not released on io_setup/eventfd failure, but free(ep_path) happens before io_setup) right (aio_multibuff.c:284-291); the old parenthetical lumped all error paths together. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of aio_simple.c (lines 222-386; the slice began inside it). It returns 1 after a message if argc != 2 or the malloc of ep_path fails. It opens "<argv[1]>/ep0" (failure returns 1), writes the descriptors and strings to it (a write returning < 0 returns 1), then in a loop opens "<argv[1]>/ep1" and "<argv[1]>/ep2" into ep[0] and ep[1] (a failure prints 'unable to open ep%d' with the file number 1 or 2 and returns 1). All those returns leave ep_path and the already opened descriptors unreleased. It then frees ep_path, calls io_setup(2, &ctx) and eventfd(0, 0), each failure printing a message and returning 1 (descriptors open, the aio context not destroyed after an eventfd failure). It mallocs buf_in, buf_out, iocb_in and iocb_out without checking them. It then loops on select over ep0 and the eventfd: select failing with errno other than EINTR breaks the loop; ep0 activity goes to handle_ep0, which sets the 'ready' flag; until ready is true the loop continues; when the eventfd is readable it reads it (a failed read breaks the loop), reaps events with io_getevents(ctx, 1, 2, ...) and clears req_in or req_out according to which endpoint the completed request used; if the IN transfer is not outstanding it prepares a pwrite of buf_in on ep[0] with eventfd notification and submits it, and likewise a pread of buf_out on ep[1] for OUT (a failed io_submit is only printed). After a break it calls io_destroy, frees the four buffers, closes ep[0], ep[1] and ep0 and returns 0.
